title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not by Grothendieck. It is page 160 of an English typescript, scanned upside down, that has been misfiled among the 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' notes. The content matches J. Lipman, 'Rational singularities, with applications to algebraic surfaces and unique factorization' (Publ. Math. IHES 36, 1969), §25. The numbering fits that paper: Remark 16.2 (desingularization when the completion is normal), 17.2/17.3 (UFD iff rational singularity with trivial class group H(R)), Proposition 22.5 (multiplicity via the configuration diagram), and the case analysis 'CASE Vd of §24'.

The theorem being proved: let R be a two-dimensional normal local ring with algebraically closed residue field k, of characteristic ≠ 2 at least in this step. Then the following are equivalent: (i) R is a non-regular UFD; (i)' its completion R̂ is a non-regular UFD; (ii) R̂ ≅ k[[X,Y,Z]]/(Z²+Y³+X⁵). This is the E8 singularity, the unique non-trivial factorial complete two-dimensional normal local ring.

Steps on this page:
1. (i)⇔(i)' follows from the desingularizability criterion and the characterization of factoriality as 'rational singularity plus trivial H(R)'.
2. For (i)⇒(ii): triviality of H(R) together with an algebraically closed residue field forces all exceptional curves to have self-intersection data '1'. The multiplicity proposition then gives multiplicity 2.
3. The classification of §24 puts R in CASE Vd. There the equation has the form z² + αy³ + tx⁴y + βx⁵ + px³z + qx²y² + rxyz + sy²z = 0, with α, β units.
4. Completing the square, z' = z + (p/2)x³ + (r/2)xy + (s/2)y², removes the z-linear terms, so one may take p = r = s = 0.

The page belongs to a proof that ends in Brieskorn's and Lipman's characterization of E8 as the only factorial rational double point.
errors: No mathematical error. The completion of the square needs 2 to be invertible (characteristic of k ≠ 2), which this step tacitly uses.

The cross and square terms are absorbed correctly. p²x⁶/4 goes into the x⁵ coefficient; s²y⁴/4 and rsxy³/2 go into the y³ coefficient; r²x²y²/4 and psx³y²/2 go into q; prx⁴y/2 goes into t. Hence α' ≡ α and β' ≡ β mod m.

ideas.what: Characterization of the E8 singularity z²+y³+x⁵ as the unique non-regular factorial complete 2-dimensional normal local ring (algebraically closed residue field)
ideas.modern_name: Factorial surface singularities; E8 is the only factorial rational double point (Mumford–Brieskorn–Lipman)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford (1961, topological version), Brieskorn (1967, char 0), Lipman (1969, general)

ideas.what: Eliminating z-linear terms in a double-point equation by completing the square
ideas.modern_name: Tschirnhaus / completing the square in a Weierstrass-type normal form

missed.claim: This page is a misfiled page of Lipman's 1969 IHES typescript on rational singularities and unique factorization (§25, E8 theorem). It is placed inside Grothendieck's cote 15 on the motivic Galois theory notes. It is an archival misattribution, not a Grothendieck result.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Archive cataloguers and readers should not attribute this content to Grothendieck. Its presence possibly reflects Lipman's preprint circulating at IHES around 1968.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of a known published paper by Lipman, misfiled. Its content is standard and fully published.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down; the transcription correctly reads it rotated.
'where ρ is a non-unit i.e. ρ ∈ (x,y,z)R' should read 'where p is a non-unit i.e. p ∈ (x, y, z)R'. The non-unit is the coefficient p, not ρ.
